article_title: Conspicuous Strategies in Teaching Expressive Writing: A Quantitative Study Comparing Two Approaches to Process Writing
citation: Fontenot, J., Carney, K. J., & Hansen, K. (2015). Conspicuous Strategies in Teaching Expressive Writing: A Quantitative Study Comparing Two Approaches to Process Writing. Journal of Instructional Research, 4. https://jir.gcu.edu
title: Conspicuous-strategy writing lesson pattern: oral rehearsal, scaffolded organizers, and three-stage editing
description: This lesson-level pattern sequences a writing lesson so that oral language precedes written production: students "talk aloud" their stories before writing and talk their paragraphs out to partners before writing and during editing. A color-coded blueprint form organizes ideas into paragraphs, providing concrete and visual support for students who need scaffolding while remaining optional for those who do not. Editing occurs three times — self-editing with a class-created rubric, peer editing, and teacher conferencing — allowing individualized instruction at each student's own level of understanding the writing process.
requirements: Teachers must be taught to use explicit instruction in highly interactive lessons
constraints: The blueprint scaffolding is not required for students who already understand the paragraph-organization process
target_learners: students requiring scaffolding at the paragraph-organization level
examples: In the study, School A students talked their paragraphs to partners before writing and during editing, and all writing received an authentic outcome through publishing
key_sources: Fontenot, J., Carney, K. J., & Hansen, K. (2015). Conspicuous Strategies in Teaching Expressive Writing: A Quantitative Study Comparing Two Approaches to Process Writing. Journal of Instructional Research, 4. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1127709

article_title: Efficacy and efficiency of indoor nighttime human external cargo mission simulation in a high-fidelity training Centre.
citation: Pietsch Urs, Lischke Volker, Sollid Stephen J. M., Prückner Stephan, Theiler Lorenz, Greif Robert, Albrecht Roland. (2020). Efficacy and efficiency of indoor nighttime human external cargo mission simulation in a high-fidelity training Centre. Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13049-020-00755-4
title: BWZSA indoor HEC night simulation facility with crane-suspended helicopter mock-ups and alpine terrain structures
description: The Mountain Rescue Centre Bad Tölz (BWZSA) houses "two specially developed three-axis cranes that suspend two full-scale mock-up helicopter fuselages", simulating flight at about 20 m altitude, with a rescue hoist and double cargo hook allowing standardised training of the full range of HEC manoeuvres. A suspended cableway with chairlift and gondola lift plus terrain structures (boulder, rock ridge, cave, uneven surfaces) supports close-to-reality alpine scenarios.
requirements: Certified simulation instructors for structured debriefing
Standard operating procedures on which scenarios are based
constraints: Some aspects of mountain rescues, such as downwash, cannot be simulated
target_learners: HEMS crew members training for nighttime winch operations
target_learning_goals: Emergency procedures such as radio failure and fixed winch-cable
examples: The facility allowed training and supervision of standard and emergency procedures such as radio failure and fixed winch-cable in a safe environment.
